text:
Lotte Hotels & Resorts hosted its annual kimchi-making event for foreign ambassadors in Korea at its Signiel Seoul hotel on Monday, introducing the diplomats to Korea's traditional food culture and spirit of sharing ahead of Kimchi Day on Sunday, the hotel operator said Thursday.
Now in its second year, the event brought together 35 ambassadors to Korea to experience "kimjang," Korea's traditional winter kimchi-making and sharing practice, which was recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage in 2013.
Lotte said the program showed Korea's spirit of sharing, with neighbors coming together to prepare food for winter.
After making the kimchi, participants received a portion of their freshly made batch packed in "onggi," traditional Korean earthenware jars, so they could enjoy it at home. Lotte Hotels & Resorts plans to collect photos of the ambassadors pairing the kimchi with their respective cuisines to create a commemorative album.
The remaining kimchi will be stored and fermented separately to be served at a welcoming dinner for newly appointed ambassadors in January, they added.
Following the hands-on session, the diplomats were treated to a special Korean dinner featuring classic kimjang-season dishes such as "suyuk" (boiled pork slices) paired with fresh kimchi, white rice and mallow soybean paste soup.
The menu also incorporated seasonal local ingredients, including porridge made with rice and seasonal vegetables, as well as yuzu mousse and Sancheong strawberry tarts.
"It is deeply meaningful that so many ambassadors joined us again this year to directly experience traditional Korean culinary culture and the value of sharing," a Lotte Hotels & Resorts official said. "We will continue to communicate and expand exchanges with foreign envoys through various programs that promote Korean culture."
Lotte Hotels & Resorts has been actively engaging with the diplomatic community through culinary programs. In April, it invited envoys from around 20 nations to the Grand Lotte Seoul hotel for a hands-on session making "gujeolpan," a traditional royal court dish served on a platter of nine sectioned plates, followed by a Korean banquet.
